literal: Gong Shun, son of Zheng Shan, was early known for his literary learning.
idiomatic: Gong Shun, son of Zheng Shan, won notice early for his literary gifts.

literal: In Wuping he was seal-letter gentleman and attendant at the Wenslin Hall.
idiomatic: In Wuping he served as seal-letter gentleman and as an attendant at the Wenslin Hall.

literal: With Cui Junqia of Boling and Li Shishang of Longxi he was united in mind and friendship; following the imperial progress to Jinyang they lodged in a monk's temple. Court men called them "the Three Youngsters of Kang Temple," and public opinion ranked them highly.
idiomatic: He was close in spirit with Cui Junqia of Boling and Li Shishang of Longxi. When the court went to Jinyang they lodged together in a monastery, and colleagues dubbed them "the Three Youngsters of Kang Temple"—a name the age endorsed.

literal: Zheng Zhengda's younger cousin by the father's line was Xiyu; his father was Daoshu.
idiomatic: Zheng Zhengda's younger cousin Xiyu was the son of Daoshu.

literal: Because his elder brother Daojiang yielded the enfeoffment, Xiyu thereby inherited Baron of Gu'an.
idiomatic: His elder brother Daojiang yielded the title, and Xiyu thereby inherited the barony of Gu'an.

literal: Empty and mild, he kept the Way, had the air of the ancients, and was respected by kin and affines.
idiomatic: Withdrawn and steady, he held to the Way with an antique bearing, and kin and affines held him in esteem.

literal: Lu Qian's elder cousin by the father's line Sunzhi was son of Wei Minister of Works Yixi.
idiomatic: Lu Qian's elder cousin Sunzhi was the son of Wei Minister of Works Yixi.

literal: Pure and quiet, few desires; he died as recorder in the Grand Tutor's establishment.
idiomatic: Pure, quiet, and sparing in desire, he ended his days as recorder in the grand tutor's office.

literal: Cui Jie, styled Yanxuan, was originally a man of Qinghe.
idiomatic: Cui Jie, styled Yanxuan, came from Qinghe.

literal: His great-grandfather Kuang crossed south of the Yellow River and settled in eastern Qing province. When the Song house established Ji province south of the Yellow River and set commanderies and counties, he thereby became a man of Eastern Qinghe commandery.
idiomatic: His great-grandfather Kuang crossed the Yellow River southward and settled in eastern Qing province. When the Song regime set up Ji province south of the river with its commanderies and counties, the family became men of Eastern Qinghe.

literal: When Nan county was divided and changed, he became moreover a man of Beiqiu in southern Pingyuan.
idiomatic: When Nan county was redivided, they were reckoned instead as men of Beiqiu in southern Pingyuan.

literal: For generations they were a great clan of the Three Qi.
idiomatic: For generations they ranked among the great clans of the Three Qi.

literal: His grandfather Lingyan was Song governor of Changguang.
idiomatic: His grandfather Lingyan had been Song governor of Changguang.

literal: His father Guang was Wei Grand Guardian.
idiomatic: His father Guang had been Wei grand guardian.

literal: Jie in youth was pure and empty, few desires, loved learning, and had family style.
idiomatic: From youth Jie was spare in wants, loved study, and carried the family's scholarly tone.

literal: At the end of Wei, from staff gentleman in the opening office he passed through gentleman of ritual observances in the ministry, secretariat director, compiler of the Veritable Records, and secretariat vice-director.
idiomatic: Late in Wei he rose from staff gentleman in an opening office through ritual observances in the ministry, secretariat director, compiler of the Veritable Records, and secretariat vice-director.

literal: In the third year of Xinghe, concurrently irregular-attendant cavalier attendant, envoy to Liang.
idiomatic: In the third Xinghe year he was also irregular-attendant cavalier attendant and sent as envoy to Liang.

literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, for discussing the abdication and change of dynasty, he was made gentleman of the yellow gate, added national university libationer, direct in the inner court, managing secrets.
idiomatic: At the opening of Tianbao, for his part in debating the abdication and dynastic change, he was made gentleman of the yellow gate, named national university libationer, and placed in the inner court to handle secrets.

literal: Pure, frugal, diligent, and careful—he was greatly known to Emperor Xianzu.
idiomatic: Frugal, diligent, and careful, he won deep notice from Emperor Xianzu.

literal: He was appointed governor of Southern Qing province; in office he had administrative achievements.
idiomatic: Appointed governor of Southern Qing, he governed with clear results.

literal: In Huangjian he entered as director of the secretariat, grand rectifier of Qi province, transferred to director of the Honglu, moved to merged-bureau director of revenue in the masters of writing, soon given capital office, soon transferred to director of the five armies in the masters of writing, supervised the national history; within the terrace pavilions he was called simple and upright.
idiomatic: In Huangjian he entered as secretariat director and grand rectifier of Qi, then director of the Honglu, then merged-bureau director of revenue, soon given a capital post, then director of the five armies while supervising the national history. Within the terrace offices he was praised as plain and correct.

literal: When Emperor Shizu was about to abdicate to the Later Sovereign, he first asked Jie; Jie remonstrated that it could not be done; thereby going against his intent, he was sent out as governor of Southern Yan.
idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu prepared to yield the throne to the Later Sovereign, he first consulted Jie. Jie urged that it must not be done; the advice crossed his will, and Jie was sent out as governor of Southern Yan.

literal: On returning from replacement, he was again made director of revenue and peer of the three ranks, with fief income from Wen commandery dry.
idiomatic: Recalled from the province, he was again director of revenue and peer of the three ranks, drawing salary from Wen commandery dry.

literal: Soon he was made secretariat director, added an open office, attendant at the Wenslin Hall, supervising compilation of the new book.
idiomatic: Soon he was secretariat director with an open office, attended at the Wenslin Hall, and supervised compilation of the new book.

literal: He met illness and died, aged sixty-six at the time.
idiomatic: He fell ill and died at sixty-six.

literal: Posthumously he was given governor of Qi, right vice director of the masters of writing, posthumous name Wenzhen.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was made governor of Qi and right vice director of the masters of writing, with the posthumous name Wenzhen.

literal: At first He Shikai monopolized the court and curried reputation by devious means; the various dukes therefore quite sought offices and stipends for their sons. Sons of eminent gates mostly held capital offices, while Jie's two sons Gong and Zong both held outer appointments.
idiomatic: At first He Shikai dominated the court and courted praise by crooked means, so great families pressed for offices and stipends for their sons. Scions of eminent houses mostly held capital posts, but Jie's sons Gong and Zong both served in the provinces.

literal: His younger brother Kuozhi said at ease to Jie: "Gong and Zong are lucky to be no ordinary men—why are they not in the provincial offices and pure eminent posts, but both go to outer provinces, harming the family line for generations?"
idiomatic: His younger brother Kuozhi said privately to Jie, "Gong and Zong are plainly gifted—why keep them out of the capital's pure offices and send them both to the provinces, to the family's hurt for generations?"

literal: Jie said: "Since establishing myself I have been ashamed to advance by a single word; now if I promote my sons, how does that differ from me?"
idiomatic: Jie said, "All my life I have been ashamed to advance by a single word of favor. If I now push my sons forward, how is that different from pushing myself?"

literal: In the end he sought nothing.
idiomatic: In the end he asked for nothing.

literal: Those who heard all sighed in admiration.
idiomatic: All who heard it sighed in admiration.

literal: Gong, in Tiantong, served Prince of Rencheng Gao Chun as staff deliberator and managed the records office.
idiomatic: Gong, in Tiantong, was staff deliberator to Prince of Rencheng Gao Chun and ran his records office.

literal: Hui was Yangzhou recorder.
idiomatic: Hui served as Yangzhou recorder.

literal: Kuozhi was deep and retiring, with discernment, and was famed for scholarship.
idiomatic: Kuozhi was reserved and discerning, famed for scholarship.

literal: From magistrate of Linshui he became western-pavilion libationer in Prince of Langye Yan's grand marshal establishment, then moved to merit staff in the guard corps.
idiomatic: From magistrate of Linshui he rose to western-pavilion libationer under Prince of Langye Yan's grand marshal, then to merit staff in the guard corps.

literal: He died in Wuping.
idiomatic: He died in Wuping.

literal: Lu Shuqi, a man of Zhuo in Fanyang, was nephew of Qing province governor Wenwei.
idiomatic: Lu Shuqi came from Zhuo in Fanyang and was nephew to Qing province governor Wenwei.

literal: His father Guangzong had will and aspiration.
idiomatic: His father Guangzong had force of character.

literal: Shuqi's two elder brothers Guan and Zhongxuan both were famed in Luoyang for their writing.
idiomatic: Shuqi's elder brothers Guan and Zhongxuan had both won fame in Luoyang for their writing.

literal: Shuqi in youth was quick-witted, bold and free, light and chivalric, loved clever stratagems, and admired Zhuge Liang as a man.
idiomatic: In youth Shuqi was quick-witted, bold and open-handed, fond of clever plans, and took Zhuge Liang for his model.

literal: Heluo Sheng appointed him long staff in the Jing province opening office.
idiomatic: Heluo Sheng made him long staff in the Jing province opening office.

literal: Sheng did not use his plans; he abandoned the city and fled to Liang.
idiomatic: Sheng ignored his plans, abandoned the city, and fled to Liang.

literal: Shuqi returned to his home county, built a chamber by the pond, and dwelt at ease in leisure.
idiomatic: Shuqi went home to his county, built a house by the waters, and lived at ease.

literal: Emperor Shizong sent a summons scroll; he pleaded illness and did not come.
idiomatic: Emperor Shizong sent a summons; he pleaded illness and stayed away.

literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was summoned again; unable to refuse, in a cloth fur robe he rode an open cart to Ye.
idiomatic: At the opening of Tianbao he was summoned again. Unable to refuse, he came to Ye in a cloth cloak aboard an open cart.

literal: Yang Yin went to visit him, intending to make him staff deliberator for the Secretariat Director; he claimed illness and would not accept.
idiomatic: Yang Yin called on him to make him staff deliberator to the director of the secretariat, but he pleaded illness and declined.

literal: When Prince Suzong took the throne he was summoned as heir apparent vice-director, added silver-blue-gleaming grand master.
idiomatic: When Prince Suzong took the throne he was summoned as heir-apparent vice-director and given the silver-blue-gleaming grand master cap.

literal: Asked about current affairs, Shuqi urged campaigning against the west, drew on the ground and stated troop dispositions, saying: "When the many face the foe, one should employ strategy; when equal, one should employ force—thus the strong can control the weak, the rich can annex the poor.
idiomatic: Asked about affairs of the day, Shuqi urged war in the west, sketched dispositions on the ground, and said, "When numbers match the enemy, use stratagem; when forces are even, use power—so the strong rule the weak and the rich absorb the poor.

literal: Now great Qi compared to the west is not the same in strong and weak, poor and rich, yet war-horses do not rest and still cannot swallow and merge them—this is the fault of not using strength and wealth.
idiomatic: Great Qi and the west are unequal in strength and wealth, yet our horses never rest and we still cannot swallow them—because we refuse to use our strength and wealth.

literal: Light troops in field battle—victory and defeat are hard to fix; that is barbarian-cavalry method, not deep planning and far calculation, the ten-thousandfold-safe art.
idiomatic: Light forces in open battle make victory uncertain—that is nomad cavalry's way, not the long-calculated art that secures all.

literal: One should establish a heavy garrison at Pingyang, facing their Pu province across, with deep moats and high ramparts, transport grain and store armor, and build fortified cities linked to it.
idiomatic: We should plant a strong garrison at Pingyang opposite their Pu province—deep moats, high walls, grain convoys, stored armor, and a chain of walled posts.

literal: If they close the passes and do not come out, then take their land east of the Yellow River; Chang'an in desperate straits will naturally starve to death.
idiomatic: If they shut the passes and hold inside, we take everything east of the Yellow River; Chang'an, cut off, will waste away on its own.

literal: If they send troops out, unless more than a hundred thousand they are not our match; the grain they supply all comes from within the passes.
idiomatic: If they march out, they need more than a hundred thousand men to match us, and every bushel they eat must come from inside the passes.

literal: Our soldiers rotate in shifts, each year one rotation; grain food is abundant and transport unbroken.
idiomatic: Our troops would rotate yearly; our granaries are full and convoys steady.

literal: If they come to seek battle we do not respond; if they withdraw their army, then seize their weakness.
idiomatic: Let them offer battle and we do not answer; let them retreat and we strike the opening.

literal: From Chang'an westward, people are sparse and cities far—enemy troops coming and going truly have hardship; holding against us, farming moreover is abandoned; within no more than three years they will break themselves.
idiomatic: West of Chang'an the land is thin of people and far between towns—every march costs them dearly. Locked with us, they cannot farm; in three years they will break themselves.

literal: The emperor deeply accepted it.
idiomatic: The emperor took the plan to heart.

literal: He also wished to place himself at Pingyang and carry out this strategy.
idiomatic: He also asked to hold Pingyang himself and carry the plan through.

literal: The sovereign ordered Yuan Wenyao and Shuqi together to plan and compile one scroll of the Pacifying-the-West Stratagem.
idiomatic: The throne ordered Yuan Wenyao and Shuqi to draft together a scroll called the Pacifying-the-West Stratagem.

literal: Before long the emperor died and the matter then slept.
idiomatic: Before long the emperor died and the scheme lapsed.

literal: When Emperor Shizu trod the throne, he was made peer of the three ranks and director of punishments in the masters of writing, then sent out as governor of He province.
idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu ascended, he was made peer of the three ranks and director of punishments, then sent out as governor of He.

literal: In Wuping he was moved to heir apparent tutor and right grand master with gleaming cap.
idiomatic: In Wuping he was moved to heir-apparent tutor and right grand master with gleaming cap.

literal: When Shuqi was in the village he had a thousand dan of grain; each spring and summer when villagers had no food he had them load and take for themselves; by autumn he left repayment to them and entirely did not calculate accounts.
idiomatic: At home Shuqi kept a thousand dan of grain. Each spring and summer, when neighbors lacked food, he let them haul what they needed; come autumn he left repayment to their conscience and kept no accounts.

literal: Yet year after year he always gained more than double.
idiomatic: Year after year he still ended with more than twice as much.

literal: Once in court eminent and honored, seeing himself old with many sons, he therefore built one great house, saying: "Here we sing; here we weep.
idiomatic: Once eminent at court, old and with many sons, he built one great house and said, "Here we shall sing; here we shall mourn.

literal: " Wei Shou once came to call on him and inquired about old matters of the Luoyang capital; before food arrived he rose, saying, "Hard to burden the host's expense.
idiomatic: " Wei Shou once called to ask about old Luoyang. Before food came he rose and said, "I hate to burden your table.

literal: " Shuqi detained him; after a long while food came—only millet meal and vegetables in wooden bowls, with a slice of dried meat only.
idiomatic: " Shuqi kept him. Long after, the meal came—millet and greens in wooden bowls and a single slice of dried meat.

literal: The attendants he brought were also all set food, each the same as this.
idiomatic: The servants he had brought were fed the same.

literal: When Qi perished he returned to Fanyang; he met turmoil and the city fell; Shuqi and clansman Shisui both died from cold porridge to the end.
idiomatic: When Qi fell he returned to Fanyang. In the turmoil the city was taken; Shuqi and his clansman Shisui both starved on cold gruel.

literal: Zhou general Yuwen Shenju, because of his fame and virtue, gathered and buried them.
idiomatic: The Zhou general Yuwen Shenju, honoring their name and conduct, gathered and buried them.

literal: Shuqi's clansman by the younger generation Chenke—his father Gui was Wei gentleman of the masters of writing and governor of Linlu commandery.
idiomatic: Shuqi's younger clansman Chenke was the son of Gui, who had been Wei gentleman of the masters of writing and governor of Linlu.

literal: Chenke's bearing was very fine; in youth he had will and aspiration, was refined in law and measure, and loved Daoist discourse.
idiomatic: Chenke's bearing was striking; young, he had purpose, kept precise habits, and loved Daoist teaching.

literal: His elder sister was consort of Prince of Rencheng; at the end of Tianbao Prince of Rencheng brought him to court, thereby promoted to heir apparent attender.
idiomatic: His elder sister was consort to Prince of Rencheng. At the end of Tianbao the prince brought him to court and had him made heir-apparent attender.

literal: He was moved to recorder in the Secretariat Director and asked leave to return and serve his grandmother Li.
idiomatic: Promoted to recorder under the secretariat director, he asked leave to go home and care for his grandmother Li.

literal: Li strongly ordered him to take office; unable to refuse, he followed the order—made heir apparent attender and heir apparent vice-director.
idiomatic: Li pressed him to serve; he could not refuse and accepted—again heir-apparent attender and then vice-director.

literal: In Wuping he was concurrently irregular-attendant cavalier attendant, envoy to Chen; on return he died on the road.
idiomatic: In Wuping he was also irregular-attendant cavalier attendant and envoy to Chen; he died on the road home.

literal: Posthumously he was given governor of Zheng and director of the Honglu.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was made governor of Zheng and director of the Honglu.

literal: Yang Xiuzhi, styled Zilie, was a man of Wuzhong in right Beiping.
idiomatic: Yang Xiuzhi, styled Zilie, came from Wuzhong in Youbeiping.

literal: His father Gu was Wei magistrate of Luoyang, posthumously given vice director of splendid happiness.
idiomatic: His father Gu had been Wei magistrate of Luoyang and was posthumously made vice director of splendid happiness.

literal: Xiuzhi was handsome and spirited, with bearing; in youth he was diligent in study, loved literary ornament, and at weak cap held the voice—the outstanding talent of his generation. You province governors Chang Jing and Wang Yannian both summoned him as provincial chief clerk.
idiomatic: Xiuzhi was sharp and high-spirited. He studied hard in youth, loved letters, and at twenty already led his generation in renown. You province governors Chang Jing and Wang Yannian both made him provincial chief clerk.

literal: In Xiaochang of Wei, Du Luozhou broke Ji city; Xiuzhi with the imperial clan and several thousand fellow townsmen fled south to Zhangwu, then on to Qing province.
idiomatic: In Wei Xiaochang, Du Luozhou took Ji. Xiuzhi fled south with kinsmen and several thousand townsfolk to Zhangwu, then to Qing province.

literal: At that time Ge Rong's bandit turmoil spread; refugees from Hebei mostly crowded into Qing.
idiomatic: Ge Rong's rebellion was raging, and Hebei refugees poured into Qing.

literal: Xiuzhi knew change was coming and therefore asked his clan uncle Boyan and others, saying: "Guest and host differ in strength; they vie to insult one another—calamity is about to arise.
idiomatic: Xiuzhi saw trouble coming and told his uncle Boyan and the rest, "Hosts and guests are unequal in power; they will bully one another until disaster strikes.

literal: As my humble view sees it, we ought secretly to return to the capital and avoid it.
idiomatic: As I see it, we should slip back to the capital while we can.

literal: " Most could not follow.
idiomatic: " Most would not go.

literal: Xiuzhi parted with tears and left.
idiomatic: Xiuzhi wept and took his leave.

literal: Soon Xing Shuo rose in rebellion; Boyan and the rest were all killed by local people, slain at one stroke—of the Yang clan several tens died, and only Xiuzhi and his brothers escaped.
idiomatic: Soon Xing Shuo rebelled. Boyan and the others were killed by locals in a single sweep; dozens of the Yang clan died, and only Xiuzhi and his brothers escaped.

literal: When Emperor Zhuang was established, he doffed commoner's garb as irregular-attendant cavalier attendant, soon in that office led the censorate, moved to attendant within the palace and recorder in the Grand Tutor's establishment, added light-chariot general.
idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang took the throne, Xiuzhi entered service as irregular-attendant cavalier attendant, soon led the censorate in that rank, then became palace attendant and recorder to the grand tutor, with the added title light-chariot general.

literal: Li Shenjun supervised the Veritable Records and memorialized that Xiuzhi, with Hedong Pei Bomo, Fanyang Lu Yuanming, Hejian Xing Ziming, and others should all enter to compile in order.
idiomatic: Li Shenjun oversaw the Veritable Records and had Xiuzhi join Hedong Pei Bomo, Fanyang Lu Yuanming, Hejian Xing Ziming, and others in the compilation.

literal: At the end of Yong'an he was, on memorial of Luozhou governor Li Hai, made champion long staff.
idiomatic: Late in Yong'an, on Luozhou governor Li Hai's memorial, he was made champion long staff.

literal: In Putai he was concurrently irregular-attendant cavalier attendant, added general who subdues the far, soon staff in Grand Guardian Sun Sui's establishment.
idiomatic: In Putai he was also irregular-attendant cavalier attendant and general who subdues the far, then joined Grand Guardian Sun Sui's staff.

literal: Soon an edict ordered him with Wei Shou, Li Tonggui, and others to revise the national history.
idiomatic: Soon an edict set him with Wei Shou, Li Tonggui, and others to revise the national history.

literal: Early in Taichang he was made gentleman of the ancestral temple section in the ministry, soon advanced to general who campaigns against the barbarians and grand master who scatters the masses.
idiomatic: Early in Taichang he was made gentleman of the ancestral-temple section, then advanced to general who campaigns against the barbarians and grand master who scatters the masses.

literal: Heluo Sheng went out as governor of Jing province and memorialized to fill the post of swift-cavalry long staff.
idiomatic: Heluo Sheng went out as Jing governor and had him appointed swift-cavalry long staff.

literal: Sheng held a mobile headquarters and again asked for him as right vice director.
idiomatic: When Sheng held a field headquarters he asked again for him as right vice director.

literal: Sheng managed Fan and Mian, and again asked for him as southern-route army marshal.
idiomatic: Campaigning on the Fan and Mian front, Sheng again asked for him as southern-route army marshal.

literal: Soon Emperor Wu of Wei entered the passes; Sheng ordered Xiuzhi to present a memorial and go to Chang'an to attend audience.
idiomatic: Soon Emperor Wu of Wei entered the passes. Sheng ordered Xiuzhi to carry a memorial to Chang'an for audience.

literal: At that time the High Ancestor also memorialized to appoint Xiuzhi vice director of splendid happiness.
idiomatic: At the same time the High Ancestor memorialized to make Xiuzhi vice director of splendid happiness.

literal: Soon, following Sheng's flight south, he still followed to Jianye.
idiomatic: Soon, when Sheng fled south, Xiuzhi followed him to Jianye.

literal: Xiuzhi heard the High Ancestor was promoting and supporting Emperor Jing; he therefore told Sheng to memorialize Liang Wu to request return. In the second year of Tianping he reached Ye and still followed the High Ancestor's order to go to Jinyang.
idiomatic: Hearing that the High Ancestor was raising and supporting Emperor Jing, Xiuzhi urged Sheng to ask Liang Wu for leave to return. In the second Tianping year he reached Ye, then went to Jinyang on the High Ancestor's command.
